headline_marked: Record turnout in Israel as [[Netanyahu faces tough test]] in wartime polls
headline: Record turnout in Israel as Netanyahu faces tough test in wartime polls
summary: Voters stream to polls in record numbers to judge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership during ongoing wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran.
details: Israelis voted in record numbers yesterday in what some call the most consequential election in the nation's history. The Central Elections Committee reported a record turnout of 66.7% by 6:00pm, with more people voting than in the entire previous election.

The election is a wartime judgment on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has led Israel through the Hamas-led attacks of October 7 and subsequent wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran. Netanyahu's right-wing coalition has been divisive at home and deepened international isolation.

His main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, aims to unseat him with support from right, center, and left parties. Opinion polls show a close race, making the path to power uncertain for both leaders.
A surge in votes from Israelis of Palestinian heritage could limit gains for Netanyahu's coalition and potentially require Arab parties' support for any government formed to oust him.
For many opponents, the election focuses on accountability for the security failures of October 7. Opposition groups have promised a national inquiry, which Netanyahu has resisted.
Netanyahu has campaigned with an endorsement from US President Donald Trump, who has urged him to 'finish the job' in the war against Iran.
If neither leader can form a governing coalition in the 120-seat parliament, Netanyahu may remain as caretaker until another election is held.

headline: 400 deaths: Dengue death toll hits 400 this year
summary: Health experts warn of delayed diagnosis and hospitalisation as October becomes the deadliest month of the outbreak.
details: At least 11 dengue patients died yesterday, bringing the total death toll for this year to 400. According to the Directorate General of Health Services, 128,237 patients have been hospitalised nationwide so far.

Medical experts note that while admissions are declining, a larger proportion of patients arriving at hospitals are critically ill. Many are arriving in shock, with undetectable blood pressure and falling oxygen saturation.
Delays in diagnosis, transportation, and admission procedures are significantly increasing the risk of death. Experts warn that delayed treatment can cause irreversible damage to vital organs.

Elderly people, those with underlying health conditions, and obese patients are identified as particularly vulnerable to severe outcomes. Severe complications like liver, kidney, respiratory, and heart failure are more common this year.

The circulation of dengue virus serotype 3 (DENV-3) and repeat infections may be contributing to the severity of the disease. Patients previously infected with dengue may be more susceptible to complications.

Doctors urge people to seek medical advice and get tested immediately if they develop fever or body aches. Patients are advised to drink sufficient fluids, including water and ORS, to prevent dehydration.

Public health experts suggest piloting free dengue testing at primary healthcare facilities to ensure timely referrals. A comprehensive approach involving community prevention and affordable early testing is needed to reduce deaths.
